rationale:
This applies card c12, Canon layers, to p11. Nothing else changes: hparams, the 256 context, learned absolute positions, the optimizer and the schedule stay the same. p19, still being screened, tests Canon-A alone on p11. To make this run a distinct measurement, it tests the card's full A+C form.

**What is added.** Each block gets two causal depthwise Conv1d layers (kernel 4, groups=n_embd, no bias), each used as a residual on the normalised input to a sublayer:
- Canon-A before attention: h = ln1(x); h = h + canonA(h); x = x + sa(h).
- Canon-C before the MLP: h = ln2(x); h = h + canonC(h); x = x + ffwd(h).

Padding is left-only, (3, 0), so position t sees only tokens t-3..t and causality holds. The weights are initialised with normal std 0.02, so each block starts as nearly the old block. The generic Xavier loop only touches Linear layers, so it will not overwrite this init.

**Mechanism.** The conv gives every token a cheap, learnable, position-aware mix of its last 3 neighbours. That covers previous-token and local n-gram features, which a 4-head × 6-layer model otherwise has to build out of scarce attention heads. Attention is then free for longer-range work: induction and copy at distance, which is what the long-range probe measures. The two convs add about 12k parameters (6 layers × 2 × 256 × 4) and very little compute.
